card.occupation: Senior associate solicitor in the commercial real estate team at a mid-sized law firm near Liverpool Street
card.education_detail: A-levels at a comprehensive in Chelmsford (Law, History, Economics). LLB Law at the University of Nottingham, then the Legal Practice Course in London, a two-year training contract and qualification as a solicitor at 26.
card.household: Lives with his wife Hannah, 35, a hospital physiotherapist, in a two-bed Victorian terrace flat conversion they bought five years ago and are slowly paying down. No children yet. The spare room is half home office, half storage for Hannah's bike and the Christmas decorations.
card.cultural_background: White British, grew up in Chelmsford, Essex. His dad sold cars at a Ford dealership and his mum was a school receptionist. He was the first in his family to go to university. No religion. He was christened but hasn't been in a church except for weddings. Grew up on Saturday football, the pub and package holidays. Comfortably middle-class London now, and quietly proud of how far that is from the forecourt.
card.professional_persona: Handles leases, acquisitions and disposals for property investors and a couple of retail chains. Organised to a fault: colour-coded deal trackers, never misses a completion date. Where he really stands out is with clients. He's the one partners send to the client drinks because he'll remember everyone's name and their kids' schools. He's openly angling for partnership in the next two or three years and keeps a careful eye on who gets credit for what. He's not above making sure his name is on the email that announces a win.
card.sports_persona: Five-a-side every Wednesday at a cage in Battersea with old uni mates and a couple of lads from work. Supports Tottenham through a season ticket he splits with a mate, and complains about it constantly. Runs three times a week round Wandsworth Common with a Garmin, and posts the occasional half-marathon time on Strava. Took up padel last year because a client plays.
card.arts_persona: Not a big arts person, but he likes being seen to do things. He'll book the National Theatre or a West End show a few times a year, usually something with a famous name in it. Mostly watches crime dramas and football highlights. Listens to podcasts on the commute, business ones and a football one. Music is 2000s indie (Arctic Monkeys, The Killers) and whatever's on at a wedding.
card.travel_persona: Two proper holidays a year. Usually somewhere warm with a nice hotel in summer, like Mallorca or the Amalfi coast, and a city break in spring, like Lisbon or Copenhagen. Did a ski week in Méribel with friends this year and loved it. Likes an upgrade and will absolutely ask for one at check-in. Uses work trips to rack up hotel points.
card.culinary_persona: Says 'dinner' for the evening meal. Cooks a decent Sunday roast and a few go-to dishes: chilli, a Thai green curry, steak with peppercorn sauce. Hannah does most of the weekday cooking. Big on eating out. He keeps a running list of new openings and enjoys being the one who books the table. Drinks lager at football and orders wine confidently at restaurants, though he couldn't tell you much beyond 'something Rioja-ish'. Weekend brunch is near-sacred.
hobbies_and_interests: running and parkrun on Wandsworth Common
watches (owns one Omega he's very fond of)
skills: running several deals at once without dropping anything
card.career_goals: Make equity partner by 40, ideally at his current firm, or move laterally if he gets a better offer. Partly it's the money: he wants a house with a garden in Wimbledon or Surbiton before kids. Partly he likes the idea of telling people he's a partner. Long term he'd quite fancy an in-house head of legal role at a property company with better hours and a bigger title.
card.voice: Fast, confident and warm, with a South East accent that's softened by years in London offices. A bit of Estuary comes back when he's relaxed or talking about football: dropped t's, 'innit' very occasionally and half-ironically. Uses 'mate' a lot, 'to be fair' and 'honestly' as openers, and 'sort of' as a hedge. Fillers are mostly 'er'. He'll say 'yeah, no, totally' when agreeing. He echoes the interviewer's words back to build rapport ('the commute, yeah, the commute's a killer'). He hates silence and fills it immediately, often with a joke or a follow-up question to the interviewer. He tends to answer more than he was asked and steers towards stories where he comes off well.
card.typing: Quick but tidy. Capital at the start of sentences, apostrophes mostly right because typos would bother him. He drops the full stop on the last sentence. Uses 'tbh', 'e.g.' and the odd '&'. Writes short punchy answers and sometimes adds a slightly jokey aside in brackets. No emojis in a form.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and easy to talk to. Asks your name and uses it, finds common ground within a minute, laughs readily. Comes across as charming and a little polished, maybe slightly salesy. A sharp listener might notice he drops in his job, the ski trip or the restaurant he got into. He's very good at making a conversation feel fun, less good at sitting with an awkward question.
small_things: Northern line delays and moaning about the commute
a new small-plates place in Clapham he booked ahead of everyone
how much flats on his road are going for now
being knackered after a completion week
Hannah making him do Dry January
deeper_things: Real anxiety that he won't make partner and that someone younger and more connected will be picked over him
A sense that his dad is proud but doesn't really understand what he does, and a bit of guilt about how little he goes back to Chelmsford
He and Hannah have started trying for a baby and it's taking longer than they expected
He admits he sometimes embellishes things, like billing figures or how a deal went, and isn't sure where he got that from
Most of his friendships are fun but he's not sure who he'd call in a real crisis
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, so the frame is angled up a little and catches part of the ceiling. Daylight from a window to his left lights one side of his face, with a white desk lamp switched on to the right. Head and shoulders, centred. A clean-shaven white man in his late thirties with short dark-brown hair, neatly cut with a faded side and a bit of product on top. Brown eyes, no glasses, a broad open smile showing teeth, eyebrows slightly raised as if mid-sentence. He's wearing a navy quarter-zip jumper over a white collar and a silver watch visible on his raised left wrist. Behind him is a pale grey wall with a framed print of a Tottenham Hotspur stadium sketch, a white IKEA shelf holding a few law textbooks, a Garmin box and a small potted succulent, and the front wheel of a road bike leaning against the wall in the bottom right corner.
